problem:
The fourth-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)$ about $x=0$ is given by

$$
{P}_{4}(x)=x-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}+\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}-\frac{1}{4}{x}^{4}.
$$

What is ${f}^{(4)}(0)?$

examples.knowledge_point: Obtaining a Higher-Order Derivative Of a Function Given its Higher-Degree Taylor Polynomial
examples.problem:
The fourth-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)$ about $x=0$ is given by

$$
P_4(x) = 1+2x-3x^2+4x^3-5x^4.
$$

What is $f^{(4)}(0)?$
examples.worked_solution:
The coefficient of $x^4$ is given by $\dfrac{f^{(4)}(0)}{4!}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{f}^{(4)}(0)}{4!} & =-5 \\ \frac{{f}^{(4)}(0)}{24} & =-5 \\ {f}^{(4)}(0) & =-120.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: Find the fourth-degree Taylor polynomial of $-\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ about $x=\frac{\pi }{2}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The fourth-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)$ about $x=a$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{4}(x) & =f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a)+\frac{{f}^{″}(a)}{2!}(x-a)^{2}+\frac{{f}^{‴}(a)}{3!}(x-a)^{3}+\frac{{f}^{⁗}(a)}{4!}(x-a)^{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Here, we have $a=\frac{\pi }{2},$ so

$$
{P}_{4}(x)=f(\frac{\pi }{2})+{f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})(x-\frac{\pi }{2})+\frac{{f}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{2})}{2!}{(x-\frac{\pi }{2})}^{2}+\frac{{f}^{‴}(\frac{\pi }{2})}{3!}{(x-\frac{\pi }{2})}^{3}+\frac{{f}^{(4)}(\frac{\pi }{2})}{4!}{(x-\frac{\pi }{2})}^{4}.
$$

So we need to work out $f(\frac{\pi }{2}),$ ${f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}),$ ${f}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{2}),$ ${f}^{‴}(\frac{\pi }{2})$ and ${f}^{(4)}(\frac{\pi }{2}),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡(x) & ⟹ &  & f(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})=-1 \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x) & ⟹ &  & {f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})=0 \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(x) & ⟹ &  & {f}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})=1 \\ {f}^{‴}(x) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(x) & ⟹ &  & {f}^{‴}(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})=0 \\ {f}^{(4)}(x) & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡(x) & ⟹ &  & {f}^{(4)}(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${P}_{4}(x)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{4}(x) & =-1+0(x-\frac{\pi }{2})+\frac{1}{2!}{(x-\frac{\pi }{2})}^{2}+\frac{0}{3!}{(x-\frac{\pi }{2})}^{3}+(-\frac{1}{4!}){(x-\frac{\pi }{2})}^{4} \\  & =-1+\frac{1}{2}{(x-\frac{\pi }{2})}^{2}-\frac{1}{24}{(x-\frac{\pi }{2})}^{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
